final_qi.question: Could a blood serum calcium level of 2.4 mmol/L contribute to the development of nephrocalcinosis?

final_qi.long_answer: Reference: [GG_2], [GG_6]. Explanation: In reference [GG_2], a patient with medullary nephrocalcinosis exhibited total serum calcium levels at the upper range of normal or slightly elevated (2.4–2.6 mmol/L). Although [GG_6] notes that normal total serum calcium is 2.1–2.6 mmol/L and overt hypercalcemia is defined at levels over 2.6 mmol/L, the evidence implies that even a calcium level of 2.4 mmol/L—especially when other contributing factors like hypercalciuria are present—could play a role in renal calcium deposition and thus contribute to nephrocalcinosis.
